transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I just haven’t been able to shake this heavy feeling. It’s like fear and guilt all mixed together. I’m tense most of the day, like I’m waiting for something else to go wrong, and I keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?

Yeah. Most nights I’m awake for an hour or two, just replaying it in my head. And when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up really easily—like at every creak in the house—or from dreams where I hear him hit the ground again.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities since what happened?
Yeah, I have. I’ve been turning down jobs if they involve raised porches or second-story decks. And at home, I’ll make excuses not to talk about the repair or even look at the spot where it happened.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the moment when it happened, like it's actually happening all over again?

Yeah. Sometimes I’ll be measuring a railing, or I hear a ladder scrape, and it just hits me out of nowhere. I can see my husband falling like it’s happening right in front of me again. My stomach drops and my hands start shaking.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I’m still doing the things I usually like when I can. I haven’t noticed a big change there.
How long have you been feeling this way since your husband's accident?
About four months now. It started after my husband fell during that porch repair, and it’s just kind of stayed with me since then.
Have you noticed any decrease in pleasure when you're doing the things you usually like?
No, I wouldn’t say that. When I’m doing something I normally enjoy, I can still enjoy it. I just… maybe don’t always get to it as much, but the pleasure itself hasn’t really dropped off.
Do you feel like these memories and feelings are causing you a lot of distress?

Yes. It’s been pretty distressing. I feel like I can’t shake this heavy fear and guilt, like I’m tense all day waiting for something else to go wrong. And I keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened.
Are there specific thoughts, feelings, or memories related to your husband's accident that you try to push away or avoid thinking about?

Yes. I try not to think about the porch repair, mostly. I’ve been turning down jobs if they involve raised porches or second-story decks, because it brings it all back. And at home I’ll make excuses not to talk about it or even look over at the spot where he fell.
Do you try to push away or avoid thoughts and memories related to your husband's accident when they come into your mind?

Yes. When it comes up, I try to shut it down pretty quickly. I’ve been turning down jobs with raised porches or second-story decks, and at home I’ll find reasons not to talk about the repair or even look at the spot where it happened.
Have you noticed yourself pulling back from or having less interest in activities that were once important or enjoyable to you since your husband's accident?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I still do most of the things I need to do. I haven’t noticed a big drop in interest, exactly… it’s more that some things just feel harder now.
Have you noticed yourself having less interest in activities that were once important or enjoyable to you since your husband's accident?
I don’t think so, not in a clear way. I still do the things I usually do. Some stuff feels a little heavier than it used to, but I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped caring about things I used to enjoy.
Have you found yourself wanting to do fewer things in general since your husband's accident?

Not really, no. I mean, I still keep up with my normal responsibilities and things I usually do. I wouldn’t say I want to do fewer things overall—some days take more effort, but I haven’t noticed a big change like that.
Have you noticed yourself having less interest in social activities or hobbies since your husband's accident?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. I still see people and do my usual hobbies when I can. Sometimes I’m a little less up for it, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in them.
Have you felt less interested in activities that usually bring you pleasure since your husband's accident?
I don’t think so. The things I usually enjoy still feel like things I want to do. Maybe I’m a little more tired or distracted sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in them.
Have you felt like you're not looking forward to things you usually look forward to?

Not really. I still look forward to things I normally would—plans with people, time off, little things like that. I might feel distracted sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped looking forward to them.
Have you felt like you don't care about things you used to care about since your husband's accident?
No, I don’t think so. I still care about the same things—my work, my family, keeping up with people. I might get worn out or preoccupied sometimes, but it’s not like I stopped caring.
Have you felt like you've pulled back from things that are important to you since your husband's accident?

Yes, a little. I’ve started turning down certain jobs—like ones with raised porches or second-story decks. And at home I’ll kind of make excuses not to talk about the repair or even look over at the spot where it happened.
